scenarioStory.history: Patient with known asthma since childhood reports worsening shortness of breath over the past hour after a URI this week. Used her albuterol MDI four times in the last 45 minutes with minimal relief before calling 911. No fever, no chest pain, no known trigger exposure today.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old female in moderate-to-severe respiratory distress, tripod positioning, with audible wheezing and accessory muscle use. She reports overusing her rescue inhaler without relief. → Oxygen and nebulized bronchodilators given: Crew administers supplemental oxygen and nebulized albuterol/ipratropium. Despite treatment, the patient shows minimal improvement and remains in significant distress. → CPAP with in-line duoneb started: Crew escalates to CPAP with nebulized albuterol/ipratropium administered in line through a T-connector. The patient begins to show improved air movement and decreased work of breathing. → Improved on CPAP, prepared for transport: Patient remains on CPAP with in-line nebulized bronchodilator during transport, with improved oxygenation and decreased work of breathing.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Progressive shortness of breath not relieved by rescue inhaler

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old female in moderate-to-severe respiratory distress, tripod positioning, with audible wheezing and accessory muscle use. She reports overusing her rescue inhaler without relief.

scenarioEvents.name: Oxygen and nebulized bronchodilators given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew administers supplemental oxygen and nebulized albuterol/ipratropium. Despite treatment, the patient shows minimal improvement and remains in significant distress.
relatedChecklist: Administer supplemental O2 titrated to target SpO2 94-98%
Albuterol 5 mg nebulized for bronchospasm with respiratory distress
Ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized in conjunction with albuterol
Apply continuous pulse oximetry and waveform capnography

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP with in-line duoneb started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew escalates to CPAP with nebulized albuterol/ipratropium administered in line through a T-connector. The patient begins to show improved air movement and decreased work of breathing.
relatedChecklist: Initiate CPAP with nebulizer administered in-line via T-connector
Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal; do not discontinue en route

scenarioEvents.name: Improved on CPAP, prepared for transport
scenarioEvents.description: Patient remains on CPAP with in-line nebulized bronchodilator during transport, with improved oxygenation and decreased work of breathing.
relatedChecklist: Reassess respiratory status, SpO2, and EtCO2 serially en route

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP escalation delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew continues nebulized bronchodilators alone without escalating to non-invasive ventilation. The patient tires, air movement worsens, and EtCO2 begins normalizing despite ongoing tachypnea — an ominous sign of impending respiratory failure.
relatedChecklist: Recognize impending respiratory failure from normalizing EtCO2 despite tachypnea
Emergently escalate to CPAP or assisted BVM ventilation with in-line bronchodilator
